extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and patent examiners (Korea/KIPO)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules governing domestic priority (priority claims based on earlier domestic patent applications) and related examination practice under Korean patent law, plus rules on patent-term extension for regulatory approval. Covers who may claim, time and substantive requirements, amendment/withdrawal, examination steps, and effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persons who can file Application Claiming Domestic Priority
rubrics_metrics.description: A person who can make a domestic priority claim is the applicant of the prior-filed application (including a successor in title under Article 38(4) of the Patent Act). The applicants of both the prior-filed application and the later-filed application shall be identical at the time of filing the later-filed application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where an application is jointly filed, the applicants of the later-filed application shall be the same as the applicants of the prior-filed application. To prove identicalness the following items shall be identical: residential or business address of the applicants, the name or title of the applicants and the seals of the applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time Requirement for Domestic Priority
rubrics_metrics.description: A later-filed application shall be filed within one year from the filing date of the prior-filed application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When multiple prior-filed applications exist, time is calculated from the earliest filing date when amending or adding priority within the extended amendment period (see amendment rule).

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive Requirement for Domestic Priority (basis of claim)
rubrics_metrics.description: A domestic priority claim can be made based on the invention disclosed in the specification or drawing(s) originally attached to the prior-filed application; inventions disclosed other than in the claims can be the basis of the claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The prior-filed application shall be neither a divisional application nor a converted application. The prior-filed application must not have been invalidated, withdrawn or abandoned, nor a decision to grant a patent or utility model registration become final and binding at the time of filing the later application. If the prior-filed application was withdrawn/abandoned on the filing date of the later application, the priority claim is deemed valid if clearly made earlier than the invalidation time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure at Filing: statement and evidential documents
rubrics_metrics.description: A person making a domestic priority shall state the purport as well as the prior-filed application in the written patent application at the time of filing the later application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission of evidential documents for priority is not necessary; validity is determined based on the cover sheet of the prior-filed application. If relying on Article 30 provisions used at the time of filing the prior-filed application, evidential documents under Article 30(2) must be submitted within the statutory period when filing the later application unless the same documents were already submitted for the prior-filed application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of Domestic Priority Claim (retroactive filing date for identical inventions)
rubrics_metrics.description: For inventions identical with those disclosed in the specification or drawings of the prior-filed application, the later-filed application is deemed to have been filed at the time of filing the prior-filed application when applying certain statutory provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically affects application of: Article 29(1),(2) Novelty and Inventive Step; Article 29(3) main sentence (enlarged concept of novelty); Article 30(1) (exception to public disclosure); Article 36(1)-(3) (first-to-file rules); Article 96(1)(3); Article 98; Article 103 (prior use non-exclusive license); Article 105(1),(2); Article 129 (presumption of process); Article 136(5) (trial for correction).

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple Priority Claim / Double-recognition prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a prior-filed application contains a domestic or Paris Convention priority claim, recognizing priority twice for inventions disclosed in the basis application would effectively extend the priority period and thus such repeated recognition is not acknowledged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effects of the priority claim instead apply to inventions newly added to the prior-filed application. To enjoy effects on the basis application's disclosed inventions, multiple priority claims must be made based on the basis application of the prior-filed application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior-filed application deemed withdrawn after 1 year 3 months
rubrics_metrics.description: The prior-filed application to which priority is claimed is deemed withdrawn when one year and three months have elapsed from its filing date, subject to exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions include where the prior-filed application has been abandoned, invalidated, or withdrawn, or where a decision to grant or a trial decision to reject has become final and conclusive, or where the priority claim based on the prior-filed application has been withdrawn. For multiple prior-filed applications, withdrawn status is determined per application from each filing date, not simultaneously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal rules for later-filed application and priority claim
rubrics_metrics.description: A later-filed application claiming domestic priority can be withdrawn at any time, but the domestic priority claim cannot be withdrawn after one year and three months from the filing date of the prior-filed application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a later-filed application is withdrawn within one year and three months from the filing date of the prior-filed application, the domestic priority claim is deemed withdrawn simultaneously. If withdrawn earlier and then priority withdrawn, special timing rules apply; an amendment copy containing all amended features suffices as a notice when changing priority claims (no separate withdrawal notice required).

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment/Additions to Domestic Priority Claim (timing and eligible persons)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may amend or add the domestic priority claim within one year and four months from the filing date of the prior-filed application (earliest filing date if multiple prior-filed applications exist).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only the applicant who fulfilled Article 55(1) and made the priority claim at filing can amend/add. Applications that may be added must meet Article 55(1) requirements: (①) prior filed within one year before later filing; ② prior not divisional/converted; ③ prior not invalidated/withdrawn/abandoned and no final grant decision; ④ applicants identical; ⑤ priority-related items clearly written. The time to determine requirement ① is at filing of later application; requirements ③ and ④ are judged at time of amendment. Priority claims based on theoretical or unspecified third-party applications are inherently invalid and cannot be added.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of amendment to priority claim and limits after deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Within one year and four months from the prior-filed filing date, amendment can include whole or partial withdrawal of priority claims in multiple claims, correction of clerical errors, and adding priority claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority claim cannot be withdrawn once one year and three months have elapsed (Article 56(2)). After one year and four months only clerical-error corrections are permitted, similar to Treaty-based priority amendments. When adding a domestic application to multiple priority claims, the relevant earliest filing date rule applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formality Examination of Domestic Priority Claim
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon submission of an application claiming domestic priority or a written amendment, the examiner shall examine the formalities of the priority claim based on the specification and written amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If errors in formality are found, the examiner requests amendment; if irregularities persist the examiner invalidates the procedure for the domestic priority claim. The formality examination covers all requirements of the domestic priority claim except unity of invention. The scope allowed for amendment may change depending on whether one year and four months has elapsed from the prior-filed filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior-art search and per-invention determination of identity
rubrics_metrics.description: After formality clearance, the examiner performs prior-art searches. If prior art related to Article 29 or 36 exists between the prior and later application, the examiner determines by invention whether each invention in the prior-filed application is identical to inventions in the later-filed application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identical inventions are examined based on the retroactive filing date; non-identical inventions prompt notice to the applicant of the reasons for not granting the retroactive filing date along with grounds for rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formalities when international application enters national phase claiming domestic priority
rubrics_metrics.description: When an international application claiming priority based on a domestic application enters the national phase (or designating only Korea), the examiner shall determine if the prior-filed application was pending at the time of the formality examination, since such a priority is deemed domestic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the prior-filed application was invalidated, withdrawn, abandoned, or a decision to grant became final at the filing date of the international application, the examiner shall request amendment; if not remedied the priority claim shall be invalidated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive examination when domestic priority is invalidated
rubrics_metrics.description: If the domestic priority claim is invalidated due to irregularities, the examiner shall examine the application based on the actual filing date rather than retroactively for patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When domestic priority is invalidated, the prior-filed application is not deemed withdrawn; examiners must be careful in applying Article 36 as the prior-filed application may still be relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive examination when domestic priority is valid (per-invention retroactivity)
rubrics_metrics.description: When domestic priority is validated, the examiner shall consider retroactive calculation by invention: inventions disclosed in the prior-filed specification/drawings are treated as if filed on the prior-filed application date for Article 29 patentability determinations; inventions not disclosed are examined on the later-filed date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This mirrors Treaty priority practice and requires per-invention identity determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instruction to defer examination of prior-filed application when domestic priority claimed
rubrics_metrics.description: When an application claims domestic priority, the prior-filed application which forms the basis is deemed withdrawn after one year and three months from its filing date; therefore, the examiner shall not start the examination of the prior-filed application but defer examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The same deferral applies where expedited examination is requested on the prior-filed application. If priority claim later found invalid, the examiner must change examination status and resume examination of the prior-filed application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant identity verification and consequences for invalid priority
rubrics_metrics.description: The person allowed to claim domestic priority is the applicant of the prior-filed application (and successor in title). If the name of the prior-filed applicant was not changed to match the later applicant before filing, the priority claim shall not be valid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicants are not identical, the examiner shall require amendment; inability to prove succession results in invalidation of the priority claim. If invalidated, the later-filed application is treated as a regular application without priority and related procedural status changes must be made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Term Extension eligibility (Article 89) — general rule
rubrics_metrics.description: If a patented invention prescribed by Presidential Decree must receive approval or registration under other statutes to be practiced, and it takes a long time to undergo required tests (efficacy, safety, etc.), the term of a patent may be extended once by up to five years to compensate for the period during which the invention cannot be practiced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Periods of delay attributable to the person who received the approval are excluded from the period counted for extension. Extension is a one-time measure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventions eligible for Patent Term Extension per Enforcement Decree Article 7
rubrics_metrics.description: "Invention prescribed by Presidential Decree" includes: (1) inventions on medicines which received certain approvals under the Pharmaceutical Affairs Act (limited to first approval among medicines manufactured with a new substance as effective ingredient); and (2) inventions on agricultural chemicals/raw materials registered under the Pesticide Control Act (limited to first registration among new-substance active ingredients).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only inventions specified by the Enforcement Decree qualify. If an invention corresponds to the specified categories, whether it took long to obtain approval is not considered for eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of patents eligible for term extension
rubrics_metrics.description: A patented invention entitled to registration for an extension of the patent term may include product, process, use, and composition patents as defined relative to Article 7 of the Enforcement Decree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application for extension can be filed only while the patent right is still valid. If the patent right has been invalidated/cancelled/extinguished (e.g., fee default), the extension application is invalid; if an invalidation trial is pending, the extension application may be filed. If the patent was valid at time of filing but later invalidated, applicant is given an opportunity to explain; if not addressed, the written application is returned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicable law and scope for approvals supporting extension
rubrics_metrics.description: For patent-term extension, approvals/registrations relevant must be those under specified acts (Pharmaceutical Affairs Act for medicines; Agrochemicals Control/Pesticide Control Act for agrochemicals) required to embody the patented invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inventions other than those required to obtain these statutory approvals/registrations (even if not practiced before approval under other acts) are not subject to extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination rules when multiple approvals, ingredients, or patents involved
rubrics_metrics.description: When multiple approvals are made on multiple active ingredients in a single patent, the applicant may choose one permitted ingredient for which to seek a one-time extension. When multiple approvals are made on the same active ingredient, the extension can be filed only on the initial approval. When a single approval involves multiple patents (e.g., product, process, use patents covering the same active ingredient), the term of each patented invention with respect to that approval may be extended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: (i) With active ingredients A, B, C in a single patent and three separate approvals, applicant selects one ingredient for the one-time extension; (ii) consecutive approvals for the same ingredient permit extension only on the initial approval; (iii) multiple patents implicated by one approval allow extension for each patent with respect to that approval.
